key_insight: ZFO separates “which direction to move” from “how far to move,” using first-order gradients for direction and cheap zeroth-order probes to adaptively choose the step size.
engineering_relevance: This gives LLM fine-tuning a lightweight, curvature-aware step selection mechanism that can be more stable than fixed-step training without the cost of a full line search.
method: Use a trusted first-order optimizer to set the descent direction.
Evaluate the objective at two additional points along that direction to fit a local 1D model.
Choose a bounded, near-optimal step from the model using shared-sample finite-difference curvature estimates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that across evaluated language models and datasets, ZFO often improved optimization and final performance over fixed-step first-order baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on the objective and the local model choice, so the method may require careful tuning of the search interval and model form.
paper_title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
